summary: The bill amends the Immigration and Nationality Act to create an independent Article I United States Immigration Courts system with appellate, trial, and administrative divisions, 15-year-term judges appointed by the President or the appellate division, and transferred jurisdiction over removal, asylum, bond, and related cases from the Executive Office for Immigration Review.

scores.thoughts: The bill establishes a new, independent Article I court system for immigration matters, including appellate and trial divisions, administrative structures, judicial salaries equivalent to federal district judges, staff appointments, facilities, and an independent budget process not subject to executive review. This requires new federal expenditures and infrastructure beyond the current EOIR setup, indicating a moderate expansion of government spending.
The bill contains no provisions related to taxes, tax rates, revenue collection, or fiscal policy changes.
The bill contains no provisions related to healthcare policy, coverage, or delivery systems.
The bill contains no provisions related to firearms, gun regulations, or Second Amendment issues.

The bill fundamentally restructures immigration adjudication by creating independent Article I immigration courts with enhanced due process protections, judicial independence from the executive branch, expanded jurisdiction over removal and asylum matters, and requirements for fair hearings and representation. This shifts the system toward greater procedural protections and rule-of-law safeguards in immigration proceedings.
The bill contains no provisions related to abortion access or restrictions.
The bill contains no provisions related to military or defense spending.
The bill contains no provisions related to environmental regulations or climate policy.
The bill contains no provisions related to welfare programs, food assistance, or social safety net policies.
The bill contains no provisions related to education funding, school choice, or federal education policy.
The bill contains no provisions related to drug enforcement, decriminalization, or controlled substances.

While the bill addresses adjudication of removal proceedings (which can involve criminal convictions), its core focus is on restructuring immigration courts for due process rather than altering criminal sentencing, policing, or rehabilitation policies.
The bill contains no provisions related to trade agreements, tariffs, or globalization.
The bill has indirect implications through new court expenditures but does not address deficit spending, debt reduction strategies, or fiscal priorities.
The bill contains no provisions related to LGBTQ+ legal protections or rights.
The bill contains no provisions related to foreign aid or international assistance.
The bill contains no provisions related to voting access, election integrity, or electoral reforms.
The bill contains no provisions related to technology regulation, data privacy, or digital oversight.
The bill contains no provisions related to worker protections, union rights, or labor relations.

The bill includes a reference to continuing education requirements under the International Religious Freedom Act but does not alter balances between religious exemptions and anti-discrimination protections.
